title: High Throughput Yeast Strain Phenotyping with Droplet-Based RNA Sequencing
protocol: Design the negative mask for the microfluidic channels using computer-assisted design software.
Print the mask on circuit board film with at least 10 µm resolution.
Place a clean 75 mm silicon wafer on a spin coater.
Pour about 1 mL of SU-8 onto the center of the silicon wafer.
Spin coat SU-8 2150 at 500 rpm for 30 s, followed by 30 s at 2,750 rpm for Device A.
Spin-coat SU-8 2100 at 500 rpm for 30 s, followed by 30 s at 2,500 rpm for Device B.
Place the wafer on a hotplate at 95 °C for 60 min to soft bake.
Remove the wafer from the hotplate and let it cool down to room temperature.
Place the mask on top of the wafer.
Expose under a collimator with a 190 mW, 365 nm UV LED for 2 min.
Place the wafer on a hotplate set at 95 °C for 5 min for postexposure baking.
Remove the wafer and let it cool down to room temperature.
Place the wafer in a bath of propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate (PGMEA) for 20 min.
Rinse the wafer with PGMEA followed by isopropanol.
If any opaque residue is visible, repeat rinsing with PGMEA and isopropanol.
Air dry the wafer.
Place the wafer on a hotplate at 95 °C for 3 min.
Remove the wafer and place it in a 90 mm diameter Petri dish.
Mix a 10:1 mass ratio of silicone base to curing agent for PDMS.
Degas the mixed PDMS for about 30 minutes.
Pour degassed PDMS onto an SU-8 master until it forms at least a 5 mm thick layer on top of the wafer.
Degas the PDMS on top of the wafer for about 30 minutes.
Place the wafer in a 65 °C oven to cure the PDMS for at least 80 minutes.
Cut out the cured PDMS slab from the wafer.
Punch inlet and outlet holes with a 0.75 mm biopsy punch on the PDMS slab with microfluidic features facing upwards.
Clean a 50 mm x 75 mm glass slide with isopropanol.
Remove all dust from the microfluidic features side of the PDMS slab using tape.
Expose the cleaned glass slide and the PDMS slab to 100 Pa (1 mbar O2) plasma for 1 minute.
Place the PDMS slab, features face down, onto the glass slide for bonding.
Place the slide in a 65 °C oven for at least 30 minutes to complete bonding.
Treat all microfluidic channels by flushing with fluorinated surface treatment fluid.
Bake the device in a 65 °C oven for at least 10 minutes to evaporate the fluid.
Count yeast growing in a suspension culture on a hemocytometer.
Resuspend cells in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to a concentration of about 750 k/mL.
Mix ultralow melting point agarose at 2% w/v in PBS and heat until melted at 90 °C.
Load the melted agarose mix into a syringe with an attached 0.22 µm filter.
Attach the syringe to a syringe pump placed before a space heater set to 80 °C.
Fill a syringe with the yeast suspension using a syringe pump.
Prepare a syringe filled with fluorinated oil containing 2% w/v ionic fluorosurfactant.
Connect tubing from all three syringes into the coflow drop splitter device.
Guide the tubing from the outlet into a 15 mL conical tube in an ice bucket for collection.
Flow the yeast suspension at a rate of 3 mL/h through the syringe pump.
Flow the agarose mixture at a rate of 3 mL/h through the syringe pump.
Flow the fluorinated oil at a rate of 15 mL/h through the syringe pump.
Collect about 1 mL of emulsion.
Wait an additional 5 min to allow the agarose to fully set.
Add an equal volume of 20% perfluorooctanol (PFO) in fluorinated oil to the emulsion.
Invert the conical tube a few times for mixing.
Spin down the broken emulsion at 2,000 x g for 2 min.
Remove the oil phase and add 2 mL of TE-TW buffer (10 mM Tris pH = 8.0, 1 mM EDTA, 0.01% Tween-20) to resuspend the gels.
Transfer the suspension into a new 15 mL conical tube.
Pellet down the gels.
Wash one more time in TE-TW for a total of two washes.
Remove supernatant and resuspend gels in 2 mL of media.
Transfer to a 5 mL culture tube.
Incubate at 30 °C overnight under shaking.
Transfer gels to a 15 mL conical tube.
Pellet hydrogels at 2,000 x g for 2 min.
Wash hydrogels in PBS twice.
Wash in 1x spheroplasting buffer once.
Perform a 2–50x dilution of spheroplasting enzyme in spheroplasting buffer and add 1 mL to the hydrogels.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Take the bottom 0.8 mL of hydrogel suspension and transfer into a 1 mL uncapped syringe.
Place the syringe in the 3D printed syringe holder.
Spin at 2,000 x g for 2 min.
Take 240,000 Drop-Seq beads and transfer into a 15 mL conical tube.
Pellet Drop-Seq beads by spinning down at 1,000 x g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend beads in 2 mL of 0.9x yeast lysis buffer with 500 mM sodium chloride for a bead suspension concentration of 120,000 beads/mL.
Transfer the bead suspension to a 3 mL syringe with a stir bar inserted.
Prepare a syringe containing several milliliters of 2% w/v PFPE-PEG surfactant in fluorinated oil.
Evacuate all the aqueous head of the syringe containing close-packed hydrogels and cap the syringe.
Insert the hydrogel, bead suspension, and oil syringes into syringe pumps.
Connect from the outlet tubing into a 50 mL conical tube on ice.
Flow the hydrogels at 0.4 mL/h into the device.
Flow the bead suspension at 0.4 mL/h into the device.
Flow the fluorinated oil at 1.6 mL/h into the device.
Collect ~1 mL of emulsion or run the device until there are no more hydrogels left.
Add 30 mL of 6x SSC buffer and 1 mL of PFO to the collected emulsion as stated in the Drop-Seq protocol.
Continue to follow the Drop-Seq protocol to generate cDNA from mRNA captured on beads.
Proceed with sequencing library preparation following the Drop-Seq protocol.
Analyze sequencing data according to the Drop-Seq protocol.
